blocks.text: Condo buildings in Simon Fraser Univer.

Tenure flag, stated at the top — this area's defining fact: every market home in UniverCity is LEASEHOLD PREPAID strata on a 99-year ground lease from SFU Community Trust — the land remains under SFU ownership and the Trust leases fully serviced, subdivided parcels to developers through 99-year lease agreements, so UniverCity homes are leasehold, not freehold. A current listing states the structure in MLS terms as "Leasehold prepaid-Strata" and another states "Leasehold expires in 2109" for its building.
Crescent Court by Liberty Homes — 8725 University Crescent (also 8761 University Crescent)

Two towers of 14 and 20 storeys over a 3-storey townhouse podium beside Richard Bolton Park: 185 apartments and 14 townhomes, completed 2022 per the developer-source pages and current listings, which record Apartment/Condo type. The 14 townhomes are part of this development and are not counted again below. Published rental/pet restrictions: Not confirmed from the sources checked.
The Nest by Mosaic — 9250 University High Street

A five-storey building of 80 condo units per the construction source; current listings record year built 2012, Apartment/Condo, Subdivision Name "The Nest," ownership "Leasehold prepaid-Strata," and one listing states "Pets & rental allow" with cats OK in its pet field.
Origin — 9150 University High Street

Current listings name the building "Origin," record Apartment/Condo type and cats OK in the pet field, and one listing states "Leasehold expires in 2109." Sources differ on the year built: one current listing records 2012 and another records 2013. Unit count is not confirmed.
Altitude by Hungerford Properties — 9060 University Crescent (Altitude Tower 1) and 9080 University Crescent

A concrete condo development in the heart of UniverCity; a directory records Altitude Tower 1 at 9060 University Crescent as 112 units, 14 storeys, built 2014, while listings at 9080 University Crescent record year built 2015 and describe "Pets & rentals allowed" — the year difference is the two towers' records, flagged here rather than merged.
Centre Block by Liberty Homes — 9393 Tower Road

A current listing names the building "Centre Block" by Liberty Homes in the heart of UniverCity and records a Simon Fraser Univer. condo for sale at this address. Year built, unit count and published restrictions: Not confirmed from the sources checked.
The Hub by Liberty Homes — 9009 Cornerstone Mews
A current listing names the building "The HUB" by Liberty Homes, records year built 2009, Apartment/Condo type and Simon Fraser Univer. sub-area. Unit count and published restrictions: Not confirmed.
Terraces at the Peak by Intergulf — 8940 University Crescent

Current listings name the building "Terraces at the Peak" by Intergulf, describe a concrete building in UniverCity and record Simon Fraser Univer. condos for sale at this address. Year built, unit count and published restrictions: Not confirmed from the sources checked.

items.t: The area is the top of Burnaby Mountain in the City of Burnaby, comprising the Simon Fraser University (SFU) Burnaby campus and the UniverCity residential community beside it; the board sub-area is listed as "Simon Fraser Univer." and SnapStats prints the full name as "Simon Fraser University SFU." A separate neighbouring sub-area, "Simon Fraser Hills," covers the Forest Grove side and is not this area.

Where the condo stock concentrates: in UniverCity's four neighbourhoods — West Highlands, East Highlands, High Street and the Slopes — around University High Street, University Crescent and Tower Road, south and east of campus; the OCP envisions a dense, mixed-use community on about 65 hectares allowing up to 4,536 residential units housing up to 10,000 residents at build-out.

Landmarks: the Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area surrounds the campus and community — 578 hectares, 34 multi-use trails over 28 kilometres, summit 366 metres — and shopping is centred on University High Street in the Cornerstone/High Street core.

blocks.text: Good to know about Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: SFU gave up land to create the park that surrounds you. As part of the original arrangement, SFU transferred more than 320 hectares of university land to the City of Burnaby for the Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area — the community's setting is a negotiated conservation boundary, not an accident.

There are no fee-simple lots inside UniverCity at all. Every market home is a strata unit on the 99-year prepaid ground lease, so "lot size" comparisons between buildings come down to unit size, floor and outlook rather than land.

Two buildings share the "Cornerstone" name in different tenures. The Hub strata building sits on Cornerstone Mews (counted above), while the Cornerstone building at 8950 University High Street is presented in current sources as furnished student rentals — a search on the name alone mixes strata and rental product.
The elementary school inside the community is not the catchment for every mountain address.

Altitude's two towers carry two different built years in public records. The directory records Tower 1 (9060 University Crescent) as built 2014; listings at 9080 University Crescent record 2015 — a small example of why the strata plan registration, not a listing, settles a building's age.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Simon Fraser Univer.
Streets, schools and getting around Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: UniverCity is a planned community on about 65 hectares, approved by the City of Burnaby in 1996 (OCP and zoning amendments), allowing up to 4,536 residential units in two neighbourhoods south and east of campus, housing up to 10,000 residents at build-out, built out in four neighbourhoods — West Highlands, East Highlands, High Street and the Slopes. The land remains under SFU ownership: SFU Community Trust leases fully serviced, subdivided parcels to developers through 99-year lease agreements, so UniverCity homes are leasehold, not freehold.
There are no conventional fee-simple residential lots inside UniverCity itself.

Plan and zoning frame: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan (adopted December 9, 2025, replacing the 1998 OCP Bylaw) is the citywide frame; UniverCity itself is governed by its own OCP framework dating to the 1996 approvals. City zoning is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026, in effect July 1, 2026) — never the former 1965 Bylaw No. 4742.

Schools (SD41; Ministry-listed names only): University Highlands Elementary is the elementary school inside UniverCity (LEED Gold certified; the school notes most families can walk to it in under 5 minutes); Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8800 Eastlake Drive) is the public secondary school on the mountain. The one locator run documented is for 8800 Eastlake Drive: Cameron Elementary (K–7) / Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8–12) (SD41 School Locator, run 2026-11-01) — note the locator returns Cameron Elementary for the secondary school's own address even though University Highlands Elementary sits inside UniverCity; listing copy for Slopes Mews units states University Highlands Elementary / Burnaby Mountain Secondary catchments, which is listing copy, not a locator run. Catchments for other addresses: Not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: Form B diligence (leasehold strata): a UniverCity strata is still a strata corporation under the Strata Property Act, so s. 59 applies — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. The Form B does not answer the ground-lease questions above — read both packages.

City property taxes (2026): City of Burnaby property taxes for 2026 were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: The university gave the city a mountain.

The elementary school beside you may not be your catchment school. The SD41 locator returns Cameron Elementary for 8800 Eastlake Drive — Burnaby Mountain Secondary's own address — even though University Highlands Elementary sits inside UniverCity a short walk away. Listing copy that states catchments (Slopes Mews listings name University Highlands) is copy, not a locator run.

The lease expiry is printed in listings, if you look. A current Origin listing states "Leasehold expires in 2109" in its body copy — the ground-lease term is a searchable, comparable fact between buildings, and the oldest (early-2000s) and newest buildings do not carry the same remaining term.
One development, two spellings, one count.

The community was planned whole. UniverCity's OCP allows up to 4,536 units housing up to 10,000 residents on about 65 hectares in neighbourhoods south and east of campus — the "still building out" feel (Arbour in the Slopes is the current phase) is the plan working as approved in 1996, not sprawl.
Winter is a pricing fact nobody publishes.
The 7% sales ratio is the negotiation.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: UniverCity is the condo and townhome community on top of Burnaby Mountain, beside the Simon Fraser University (SFU) campus inside its Ring Road, in the City of Burnaby.
The community covers about 65 hectares around the campus, planned as neighbourhoods south and east of SFU, reached by University Drive and Gaglardi Way from below the mountain.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: Every UniverCity home sits on SFU-owned land: buyers own the strata unit, and the land is held under a prepaid 99-year leasehold, not freehold.

Named buildings verified in the local index include Altitude, 9060 and 9080 University Crescent; Origin, 9150 University High Street; The Nest by Mosaic, 9250 University High Street; The Hub by Liberty Homes, 9009 Cornerstone Mews; and Centre Block, 9393 Tower Road — addresses as indexed, to be confirmed on title for any specific unit.
The Trust states it has developed homes for more than 5,000 UniverCity residents with Lower Mainland developers, in low-rise and tower forms around University High Street and University Crescent.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Tenure is the first rule here: SFU retains ownership of the land, and serviced, subdivided parcels go to developers through 99-year lease agreements, so a purchase is a leasehold strata interest.

Development form is set by the Simon Fraser University Official Community Plan, adopted September 9, 1996 and amended April 15, 2002, which forms part of Burnaby's Official Community Plan (OCP) and is the basis for rezoning land within the Ring Road for leasehold subdivision for market housing.
The plan allows up to 4,536 residential units, so remaining density is a plan figure, not a per-building promise; check the specific strata plan and lease for the building.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Heat and hot water billing in connected UniverCity buildings runs through the Corix district energy system, not individual gas or electric baseboards — confirm the utility charge in the strata budget.

The on-mountain elementary school leases its building from SFU Community Trust: University Highlands was converted from an existing office building and is leased to the Burnaby School District by the Trust.
Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area surrounds the community: the City lists 34 multi-use trails over about 28 kilometres across 578 hectares, with the summit at 366 metres.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area Condos and Townhomes: development and new projects

items.t: Burnaby Mountain Gondola, Production Way–University Station to SFU Burnaby campus, TransLink, transit project: the preferred Route 1 is the straight route with the terminal near the bus exchange; TransLink states the project is not yet approved or funded and must be in a future investment plan with TransLink Board and Mayors' Council approval — status: business case stage (as of November 3, 2026).

UniverCity remaining parcels, UniverCity, SFU Community Trust with parcel developers, condos, townhomes and rentals: the Trust's own 2022 update lists Oslo (Parcel 33), Crescent Court (Parcel 20), Hamilton (Parcel 19, 12 storeys), Arbour (Parcels 34 and 35, Intergulf), Parcels 36 and 37 (Rize Alliance purpose-built rentals) and Parcel 24 (Mosaic Homes) at occupancy or construction stages at that date — check current, as that update is dated June 3, 2022.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: The UniverCity-specific cost is district energy: connected buildings buy heat and hot water from the Corix Burnaby Mountain District Energy Utility rather than a municipal utility.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: SFU Exchange is the on-mountain transit hub named on TransLink's R5 timetable, and Production Way–University Station on the Millennium Line is the rail station the mountain buses feed.
Route 145 runs Production Way Station to SFU Exchange, and Route 143 runs SFU Exchange to Burquitlam Station, per TransLink timetables.
The R5 Hastings Street RapidBus runs Burrard Station to SFU, at least every 10 minutes at peak and 15 minutes off-peak, per TransLink.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University Area Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the lease first: the due-diligence document for any UniverCity unit is the 99-year ground lease and the strata's leasehold terms, because SFU retains the land — a freehold title search alone does not describe this tenure.

Check slope and watercourse conditions against the SFU Official Community Plan, which requires subdivision proposals to include a topographic survey showing watercourses and significant trees and preliminary watercourse protection proposals.

blocks.text: Simon Fraser University SFU home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

87 condos sold in Simon Fraser University SFU with a median price of $512,000 (the middle half sold between $437,500 and $606,500), taking a median of 39 days to sell at 96.8% of the last list price; 8% sold above list. They had a median $635 per square foot, a median year built of 2012 and a median strata fee of $491 a month. 7 townhomes sold in Simon Fraser University SFU with a median price of $825,000, taking a median of 34 days to sell at 96.9% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $582 per square foot, a median year built of 2014 and a median strata fee of $799 a month.

The land remains under SFU ownership; SFU Community Trust leases serviced parcels to developers through 99-year lease agreements, and buyers hold a leasehold strata interest — a current Origin listing states its lease expires in 2109. Never price or finance a unit here as freehold.
faq.q: Are UniverCity homes freehold or leasehold?

faq.a: Strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, and current listings at The Nest and Altitude state pets and rentals are allowed — but occupancy demand is heavily student-driven and the ground lease and strata documents still govern everything else, so verify building by building.
faq.q: Can I rent out a UniverCity condo long-term?

faq.a: University Highlands Elementary (SD41) sits inside the community and was designed so most families can walk to it in under 5 minutes; Burnaby Mountain Secondary is the public secondary school on the mountain.

faq.a: Not as an approved project: TransLink states the Burnaby Mountain Gondola is not yet approved or funded and still needs a future investment plan plus TransLink Board and Mayors' Council approval. Treat it as upside, not current transit.
Check each building's lease commencement on title instead of assuming.
faq.q: Does the remaining lease term affect price between old and new buildings?

faq.a: No — nothing in UniverCity is freehold. SFU Community Trust leases serviced parcels to developers through 99-year prepaid ground leases; you buy a leasehold interest in a strata unit (a current Origin listing states "Leasehold expires in 2109").

Inside the developments: Crescent Court (14 townhomes beside 185 apartments), Terraces at the Peak (townhouse units at 8980 University Crescent), Slopes Mews buildings (townhouse-form units at 9168/9228 Slopes Mews, 9888 University Crescent), and the Arbour presale's stacked townhomes (9688 University Crescent).
faq.q: So where are the townhouses on the mountain?

faq.a: Both, in that order of risk: the Form B for the strata's finances and bylaws, and the ground lease for commencement date, remaining term, prepaid status and end-of-term provisions. The lease is what a lender and lawyer will scrutinize; some lenders cap mortgage terms against the remaining lease term (general guidance — not verified per lender).
faq.q: What should I read first on a UniverCity purchase — the Form B or the ground lease?

faq.a: No — the land stays in SFU ownership. The SFU Community Trust prepares zoned, serviced, subdivided sites for private developers on a prepaid, 99-year leasehold basis, and home buyers hold strata title in the building on that leasehold land. A buyer should have a lawyer review the head lease, the remaining lease term and any lease terms that run with the strata before removing subjects.

University Highlands Elementary, at 9388 Tower Road, is the on-mountain school. It is a Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Gold school inside UniverCity, designed so surrounding residences are within about a five-minute walk, with limited parking and a two-minute parking zone on University High Street. Catchment for a specific address is still a Burnaby School District check.
faq.q: Which elementary school is on the mountain?

faq.a: Buses from SFU Exchange are the current link. TransLink lists the R5 Hastings Street RapidBus to Burrard Station, Route 143 to Burquitlam Station, Route 144 to Metrotown Station and Route 145 to Production Way–University Station from the exchange. There is no SkyTrain station on the mountain; the rail connection is at the bottom of the bus ride.
faq.q: How do residents get off the mountain without a car?

faq.a: District energy, in connected buildings. The Burnaby Mountain District Energy Utility's biomass Renewable Energy Centre, completed in 2020, provides heat and hot water to most of the SFU campus and about half of UniverCity, using locally sourced wood waste with natural gas boilers for peaking and backup. Whether a specific building is connected is a strata-documents check.
